blocks.text: You may be given a newborn and asked:

items: “Perform a gestational age assessment using the New Ballard Score.”
“Estimate the gestational age of this baby clinically.”

blocks.text: “A newborn has an uncertain gestational age. Estimate the gestational age.”

items: “Demonstrate the neuromuscular components of the Ballard score.”
“Interpret the findings and give the estimated gestational age.”

blocks.text: They want to see that you can:
Convert the total score to an estimated gestational age.
Recognise whether the baby is preterm, term or post-term.
Recognise factors that can make the assessment unreliable.
The New Ballard Score combines 6 physical and 6 neuromuscular maturity criteria. Merck Manuals
“Good morning. My name is Dr ____. I have been asked to assess this newborn to estimate the gestational age using the New Ballard Score.”

“I would like to examine the baby using some gentle movements of the arms and legs and assess a few physical features such as the skin, ears, breast tissue and genitalia. This will help me estimate the baby's gestational age. Is that okay?”
“I will keep the baby warm and stop if the baby becomes distressed.”
Do not immediately assume Ballard is the best source of gestational age.

If a reliable early pregnancy ultrasound or reliable obstetric dating is available, that information is generally more reliable. Ballard is particularly useful when gestational age is uncertain or when there is a major discrepancy between the obstetric estimate and clinical findings. Merck Manuals

subsections.subsection_title: Why do we assess gestational age?

items: Risk of sepsis and other complications
Whether the infant is SGA, AGA or LGA
Need for monitoring for complications of prematurity

subsections.subsection_title: NEW BALLARD SCORE — THE BIG PICTURE

blocks.text: “Skin, Lanugo, Plantar, Breast, Eye, Genitals — Posture, Square, Arm, Popliteal, Scarf, Heel.”
“I am assessing the skin for transparency, thickness, visible veins, peeling and wrinkling.”
Thin/translucent → smooth → peeling → thick → parchment-like → leathery/wrinkled
Very thin, translucent skin suggests prematurity.
Thick, cracked, wrinkled, leathery skin suggests advanced maturity/postmaturity.
“The skin is smooth, pink and relatively opaque with minimal visible veins, consistent with increasing physical maturity.”
“The skin is thin, translucent and gelatinous with prominent superficial vessels, suggesting significant prematurity.”
“The skin is thick, dry, cracked and leathery with marked wrinkling, suggesting postmaturity.”
Lanugo is the fine, soft hair found on the fetus/newborn.

items: “I am assessing the amount and distribution of lanugo.”

blocks.text: Lanugo does not simply increase progressively with gestational age.
It appears, becomes abundant, then gradually disappears with increasing maturity.
Absent → abundant → thinning → bald areas → mostly disappearing
“There is abundant fine lanugo over the back, consistent with an intermediate degree of physical maturity.”
“Lanugo is sparse with areas of disappearance, suggesting increasing gestational maturity.”
This is an important Ballard component.
“I am assessing the plantar surface for the presence and distribution of plantar creases.”
Smooth sole → anterior creases → creases over more of the sole → deep creases over the entire sole

items: Creases extending across most or all of the sole

blocks.text: “The plantar surface is relatively smooth with few creases, suggesting reduced physical maturity.”
“There are numerous deep plantar creases extending across the sole, consistent with greater gestational maturity.”
Describe where and how extensive the creases are.
If necessary, very gently palpate the breast tissue between thumb and finger.

items: “I am assessing the breast tissue and areolar development.”

blocks.text: Barely perceptible breast tissue → increasing breast tissue → stippled areola → raised areola → prominent breast bud

rows: Well-developed breast bud and prominent areola

blocks.text: “There is a small but clearly palpable breast bud with a developed areola, consistent with increasing physical maturity.”
Do not squeeze the breast aggressively.
This assesses mainly the ear cartilage and eyelid development.
Gently fold the upper part of the pinna forward.

items: “I am assessing the development and recoil of the pinna.”

blocks.text: “The pinna is soft and remains folded with slow recoil, suggesting reduced gestational maturity.”
“The pinna is well formed with firm cartilage and immediate recoil, consistent with greater maturity.”
This differs between male and female newborns.
“In this male infant, I am assessing testicular descent and scrotal development.”
“Both testes are descended and the scrotum has well-developed rugae, consistent with greater gestational maturity.”
Labia majora enlarge and progressively cover the clitoris and labia minora.
“In this female infant, I am assessing development of the clitoris and labia.”
“The clitoris is relatively prominent with underdeveloped labia majora, suggesting reduced gestational maturity.”
“The labia majora are well developed and cover the labia minora and clitoris, consistent with greater maturity.”
This is where candidates often lose marks because they know the names but do not demonstrate them properly.
The degree of flexion of the limbs at rest.
Do not force the limbs into position.
“I am assessing the baby's resting posture and degree of flexion.”

items: Strong flexion of arms and legs

blocks.text: “The infant lies predominantly extended with minimal flexion, indicating low neuromuscular maturity.”
“The infant demonstrates spontaneous flexion of all four limbs, consistent with good neuromuscular maturity.”
This is a classic Ballard manoeuvre.
Gently flex the hand towards the forearm.
Observe the angle between the palm and forearm.
“I am assessing the square-window sign by gently flexing the hand towards the forearm and estimating the angle.”
Hand can be flexed easily → large angle.
“The wrist demonstrates marked resistance to flexion with a small square-window angle, consistent with good neuromuscular maturity.”
Place the baby's arms in flexion.
Observe how rapidly they return to flexion.
“I am assessing arm recoil by briefly extending the upper limbs and observing the return to flexion.”
“There is minimal recoil following extension of the arms, indicating reduced neuromuscular maturity.”
“There is brisk recoil of both arms into flexion, consistent with good neuromuscular maturity.”
Flexor tone of the lower limb.
Flex the thigh towards the abdomen.
Observe the angle at the knee.
“I am assessing the popliteal angle by flexing the thigh and gently extending the lower leg until resistance is encountered.”
“The knee extends readily to a wide popliteal angle, suggesting reduced neuromuscular maturity.”
“There is marked resistance to extension with a small popliteal angle, indicating good neuromuscular maturity.”
This is another frequently tested manoeuvre.
Gently draw the arm across the upper chest like a scarf.
Observe the position of the elbow in relation to the chest.
“I am performing the scarf sign to assess passive tone of the upper limb.”
Arm crosses easily across the chest.
“The arm crosses easily over the chest with minimal resistance, suggesting reduced neuromuscular maturity.”
“There is marked resistance to bringing the arm across the chest, consistent with good neuromuscular maturity.”
Gently bring the leg towards the ear.

items: “I am assessing the heel-to-ear manoeuvre for lower-limb flexor tone.”

blocks.text: Leg moves easily towards the ear.

items: Heel remains relatively far from ear

blocks.text: “The leg can be brought readily towards the ear with minimal resistance, suggesting reduced neuromuscular maturity.”
“There is marked resistance to bringing the heel towards the ear, consistent with increased neuromuscular maturity.”
The scores are added to obtain a total Ballard score, which is then converted to estimated gestational age using the standard New Ballard chart. Merck Manuals

subsections.subsection_title: IMPORTANT: DON'T MEMORISE AN UNSAFE SHORTCUT

blocks.text: In an actual OSCE, the station may provide the Ballard scoring chart.
Use the chart supplied by the examiner.
Do not rely on an approximate mental conversion if the chart is available.

Physical score = 18 Neuromuscular score = 16 Total = 34 Using the New Ballard chart → approximately the corresponding gestational age Therefore: “The estimated gestational age is approximately ___ weeks.”
The exact conversion should be taken from the standard chart used by your institution.

items: Descended testes with good scrotal rugae

blocks.text: You score each component according to the New Ballard chart.

“I have assessed all six physical and six neuromuscular components. The total Ballard score is ____. According to the New Ballard conversion chart, this corresponds to an estimated gestational age of approximately ____ weeks.”

items: “This is therefore consistent with a [preterm/term/post-term] newborn.”

subsections.subsection_title: HOW TO REPORT TO THE EXAMINER

blocks.text: “I assessed the newborn using the New Ballard Score, comprising six physical and six neuromuscular maturity criteria. The physical findings show [brief summary], while the neuromuscular examination demonstrates [brief summary]. The total score is ____, corresponding to an estimated gestational age of approximately ____ weeks. This is consistent with a [preterm/term/post-term] infant.”

“I would correlate this with the best available obstetric dating, particularly early pregnancy ultrasound, because clinical Ballard assessment has an accuracy of approximately ±2 weeks and is less reliable in sick neonates.” Merck Manuals
That final sentence can earn you an examiner bonus mark.
You specifically want more examples of how to report abnormal findings. These are very useful for OSCEs.

“The infant has thin, translucent skin, sparse plantar creasing, poorly developed breast tissue, a soft pinna with poor recoil and predominantly extended posture with minimal flexor tone. These findings suggest significant prematurity.”

content_groups.group_title: Example 2 — Preterm with poor neuromuscular maturity

blocks.text: “The infant demonstrates reduced spontaneous flexion, poor arm recoil, a wide popliteal angle and minimal resistance on the scarf and heel-to-ear manoeuvres, indicating reduced neuromuscular maturity.”

“The infant has well-developed skin, numerous plantar creases, mature breast tissue, firm ear cartilage and well-developed genitalia, with good flexor tone throughout. These findings are consistent with a term infant.”
“The infant has thick, dry, cracked and wrinkled skin with reduced lanugo and marked plantar creasing. The physical findings suggest advanced gestational maturity and possible postmaturity.”
“The infant demonstrates reduced neuromuscular tone with poor recoil and reduced resistance to passive manoeuvres. The neuromuscular component may therefore underestimate gestational maturity.”
“I would interpret the Ballard score cautiously and correlate it with obstetric dating and the clinical condition.”

“The physical and neuromuscular findings suggest an estimated gestational age of approximately ___ weeks; however, the infant is clinically unwell, which may reduce the reliability of the neuromuscular assessment.”
Clinical illness can make neonatal clinical gestational-age assessment less reliable. Merck Manuals

“The physical maturity findings suggest approximately ___ weeks, but the neuromuscular findings should be interpreted cautiously because maternal magnesium sulphate exposure can affect neonatal tone.”
Maternal medications such as magnesium sulphate can influence neuromuscular components. Merck Manuals

“The Ballard assessment suggests approximately 34 weeks, whereas reliable early ultrasound dating suggests 38 weeks. There is therefore significant discordance, and I would favour the reliable obstetric dating while investigating the reason for the discrepancy.”

“The physical maturity assessment suggests approximately 38 weeks despite a low birth weight. This indicates that low birth weight should not automatically be interpreted as prematurity; gestational age and birth weight should be assessed separately.”
“The infant appears large for gestational age, but the Ballard findings are consistent with approximately 39 weeks. Size alone should not be used to estimate gestational age.”
“The clitoris is relatively prominent and the labia majora are poorly developed, with incomplete coverage of the labia minora, suggesting reduced genital maturity.”
“The testes are not fully descended and the scrotum has poorly developed rugae, suggesting reduced genital maturity.”
“The pinna is well formed with firm cartilage and rapid recoil after folding, indicating advanced physical maturity.”
“The pinna is soft and remains folded after manipulation with delayed recoil, suggesting reduced gestational maturity.”

content_groups.group_title: Example 15 — Discordant physical and neuromuscular scores

blocks.text: “There is a discrepancy between the physical and neuromuscular maturity scores. I would consider factors such as illness, medication exposure and growth abnormalities and would correlate the findings with reliable obstetric dating.”
The New Ballard Score was expanded specifically to include extremely premature infants, but clinical estimation still has limitations. Merck Manuals
A sick baby may appear less neurologically mature than the actual gestational age.

The New Ballard Score can be used up to approximately 4 days after birth, but it is commonly performed within the first 24 hours. Physical findings change more rapidly after birth, whereas neuromuscular components tend to remain more consistent. Merck Manuals

“No. When reliable obstetric dating is available, particularly from early pregnancy ultrasound, it is generally preferred. Ballard assessment is particularly useful when obstetric dating is uncertain or when there is a significant discrepancy.”

content_groups.group_title: Q1. What is the New Ballard Score?

blocks.text: “It is a clinical scoring system used to estimate neonatal gestational age based on physical and neuromuscular maturity.”

content_groups.group_title: Q2. How many components are assessed?

items: “Twelve components: six physical and six neuromuscular.”
“Skin, lanugo, plantar surface, breast, eye/ear and genitalia.”

blocks.text: “Posture, square window, arm recoil, popliteal angle, scarf sign and heel-to-ear.”

content_groups.group_title: Q5. What happens to flexor tone with increasing gestational age?
Q6. What happens to the popliteal angle with increasing maturity?

items: “The popliteal angle becomes smaller because flexor tone increases.”

content_groups.group_title: Q7. What happens to the square-window angle with maturity?

items: “The angle becomes smaller because resistance to wrist flexion increases.”

content_groups.group_title: Q8. What happens to arm recoil?

items: “Recoil becomes more brisk with increasing neuromuscular maturity.”

content_groups.group_title: Q9. What happens to the scarf sign?

blocks.text: “Resistance to bringing the arm across the chest increases with maturity.”

content_groups.group_title: Q10. What happens during the heel-to-ear manoeuvre?

blocks.text: “Resistance to bringing the heel towards the ear increases with maturity.”

content_groups.group_title: Q11. When is Ballard assessment less reliable?

blocks.text: “It is less reliable in very sick neonates and can be affected by factors such as medication exposure. It also has an inherent accuracy of roughly ±2 weeks.” Merck Manuals

content_groups.group_title: Q12. Can Ballard distinguish a 38-week baby from a 39-week baby reliably?

blocks.text: “Not reliably. The method has an accuracy of approximately ±2 weeks, so it should not be interpreted as precise to a single week.” Merck Manuals
Q13. What is the most important source of gestational age if reliable antenatal dating exists?

items: “The best available obstetric estimate, particularly reliable early ultrasound dating.”

blocks.text: Even though it is a newborn, still demonstrate appropriate communication with the parent.
Keep the baby appropriately covered and expose only the area being examined.
A sick baby may have abnormal tone unrelated to gestational age.
Especially maternal magnesium sulphate and sedative/anaesthetic exposure.

content_groups.group_title: ❌ 8. Calling a low birth weight baby automatically premature

blocks.text: You need gestational age + birth weight.
Always convert the score to an estimated gestational age.

content_groups.group_title: ❌ 10. Giving a falsely precise gestational age

blocks.text: “The Ballard assessment estimates approximately 35 weeks, recognising the method's approximately ±2-week accuracy.”

blocks.text: “I performed a New Ballard assessment comprising six physical and six neuromuscular maturity parameters. The infant demonstrates [brief physical findings] and [brief neuromuscular findings]. The total score is ____, corresponding to an estimated gestational age of approximately ____ weeks. This is consistent with a [preterm/term/post-term] infant. I would correlate this with the best available obstetric dating, as the Ballard assessment has an accuracy of approximately plus or minus two weeks and may be less reliable in sick neonates or following medications that affect neuromuscular tone.” Merck Manuals
The highest-yield conceptual point is that Ballard does not simply ask, “Does this baby look premature?”
PHYSICAL MATURITY + NEUROMUSCULAR MATURITY → TOTAL SCORE → ESTIMATED GESTATIONAL AGE
And when the clinical estimate conflicts substantially with reliable antenatal dating, do not automatically assume Ballard is correct. Merck Manuals
